title: Add sampled thread-window counters and mini-bench exporter for kernel-selection telemetry
author: Aditi Rao
description: Motivation: We need lower-overhead, workload-shaped telemetry to drive kernel-selection heuristics and continuous-batching policies without the cost of full-trace collection. This PR adds a platform-agnostic sampled per-thread "thread-window" counter and a tiny microbenchmark harness (mini-bench) that exercises kernel-selection hot paths under controlled tile/sequence distributions. Design: each worker thread maintains a ring buffer of fixed-duration windows (configurable, default 20ms) that aggregate op counts, queued requests, KV-cache hits, and cumulative kernel time. Windows are rotated via a lightweight atomic epoch; sampling mode optionally snapshots a single hot window per op to bound overhead. A small "pico-trace" marker API (no dependency on vendor tooling) emits compact timeline events when enabled. The mini-bench runs kernel-selection scenarios (short/long sequences, cache-warm/cold) and produces aggregated Prometheus metrics plus a compact timeline JSON export for dashboarding. Exporter: mini_perf_exporter translates per-thread window histograms into Prometheus metrics (redwood_thread_window_latency_ms, redwood_kernel_choice_count) and a compact line-oriented JSON timeline consumed by our perf-visualizer tool. Low-overhead modes: OFF/COUNTERS/SAMPLED where COUNTERS is always-on cheap counters and SAMPLED turns on window snapshots; the default is COUNTERS. Implementation notes: lock-free ring buffer (single-writer per-thread, lockless readers), small fixed allocations to avoid GC pressure, opt-in via RUNTIME_THREAD_WINDOW env/config flags; config knobs added to console/agent for Dedicated. Testing: unit tests for ring buffer correctness and race scenarios, integration mini-bench runs in CI smoke, and a small perf regression guard that fails the PR if kernel-selection latency increases >15% in smoke baseline. Backwards compatibility: opt-in, no behavior change when disabled. How to use: enable RUNTIME_THREAD_WINDOW=1 and run tools/perf/visualizer/mini-timeline-to-grafana.py to convert JSON to dashboard-friendly panels. Related: ENG-2403 (instrumentation work) and PM-612 (kernel-selection tuning).

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can you quantify the steady-state overhead in COUNTERS vs SAMPLED modes? We need an approximation for Dedicated SLAs.
Author (Aditi): Measured at -COUNTERS ~0.4% p99 token latency overhead on our small-scale smoke; SAMPLED adds ~1.5% with 20ms windows. Numbers added to description and unit smoke outputs.
Hannah Lee: I'm concerned about fairness when a thread gets hot for many consecutive windows — does the ring drop older windows deterministically?
Author: Ring is circular; we track epoch and window age. For fairness, the exporter aggregates by recent N windows (configurable) rather than single-window peaks. Added config and doc note.
Omar Khalid: Lockless readers are tricky. Tests look good but can we add an integration run that saturates batching?
Author: Added a mini-bench saturation scenario and CI smoke integration; included a transfer check to ensure no stale reads during shutdown.
Miguel Santos: Approve after you add the console toggle in a follow-up or link the UI ticket.
Author: Added console flag wiring in this PR; pinging UX for follow-up dashboard panels (PM-612).
Hannah Lee: Quick nit on naming: rename export metric to redwood_kernel_choice_count for clarity. Done.

release_notes: Adds opt-in low-overhead runtime telemetry: thread-window counters and a mini-bench exporter. Enable with RUNTIME_THREAD_WINDOW=1. Emits Prometheus metrics: redwood_thread_window_latency_ms and redwood_kernel_choice_count, and a compact timeline JSON for perf dashboards. No behavioral changes when disabled.
